Lesko Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lesko, Poland

Not demolished. From the first half of the 19th century until the Holocaust, members of the Horowic family served as rabbis and tzadiks in Lesko; the most famous, Naftali Cwi Horowic (1760–1827), was born in the town before settling in Ropczyce. This cemetery, in use from the 1540s until the Holocaust, saw the Soviet occupiers of 1939–41 remove tombstones made of valuable stone, with German occupiers later using others for construction. Over 2,000 matzevot survive, including about 100 from the 16th and 17th centuries, the oldest dated 1548; the cemetery was entered into the Register of Monuments in 1969.
